samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Yo, check it out.
Sunday night, sports hall, badminton lines on the floor.
Two rigs, one referee, one fire door.
Cut this plate on Thursday, one-off acetate.
Bass so low the scoreboard starts to vibrate.
Your selector's sweating and I've not started, mate.
Needle down, hand up, that's the first one gone.
Rewind!

[Chorus]
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
Sports hall soundclash, ready, go.
One dubplate and your tweeters bl—

[Verse 2]
Second plate, drop it, that's the horn section.
Your stack's got a wobble, mine's got direction.
Tweeters ticking, your crossover's cooked.
Paper cones flapping like a phone book.
I'm the rig wrecker, the tweeter executor.
The mid-range mangler, the woofer persecutor.
Prodigy on the mic and the hall's overbooked.
Check it.

[Chorus]
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
Sports hall soundclash, ready, go.
One dubplate and your tweeters bl—

[Verse 3]
Third plate, last plate, this one's the ender.
Horns smoking, amps in surrender.
Ref's got the plug in his hand, shaking.
Six hundred heads, floorboards quaking.
Your bass bin's a wardrobe now.
Your tops are toast, take a bow.
Pull it, ref, pull it, they're done.
Prodigy took the hall, and the clash is won.

[Chorus]
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
Sports hall soundclash, ready, go.
One dubplate and your tweeters bl—

[Interlude - Spoken]
Channel one, check. Channel two, check.
Left stack, right stack, check.
Plate three, cue it.

[Chorus]
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
One dubplate and your tweeters blow.
Sports hall soundclash, ready, go.
One dubplate and your tweeters bl—

[Outro - Instrumental]
samples.title: Sports Hall Soundclash - Fable 5.1

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Do you want the cheese one? Do you want the ham?
Auntie Pat is asking who I am.
He's got my keys in his coat, he's got my flat,
He's got the freckle I could draw with my eyes shut.
Everybody's lovely, everybody's fine,
Everybody's holding out a glass of wine.

[Pre-Chorus]
I could say it in a second,
It would only take a breath.
But my mother's turning seventy,
And I'm a coward in a nice shirt.

[Chorus]
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Give him the smallest slice.
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Hasn't the weather been nice?
Seventy candles and a hired van,
And a lie the size of the room.

[Interlude]
More cake, anyone?
Lovely. Lovely.

[Verse 2]
Do you take sugar? Do you take two?
Cousin Danny wants to know your name.
So he says it, and she writes it on a card,
Filed with the others, all the boys who came.
Thirty-eight years old in a paper hat,
Saying, 'Yes, we share the rent, and that is that.'

[Pre-Chorus]
He is holding my hand under the table,
Where the tablecloth is long.
And the awful thing, the awful thing,
Is I've done this for so long.

[Chorus]
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Give him the smallest slice.
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Hasn't the weather been nice?
Seventy candles and a hired van,
And a lie the size of the room.

[Bridge]
Ask me. Ask me.
Go on, ask me one more time.
Ask me. Ask me.
And I'll tell you he is mine.

[Chorus]
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Give him the smallest slice.
This is my flatmate, mother, this is my flatmate,
Hasn't the weather been nice?
Seventy candles and a hired van,
And a lie the size of the room.

[Post-Chorus]
(Lovely, lovely, isn't it lovely.)
(Lovely, lovely, pass the plate.)
(Lovely, lovely, isn't it lovely.)
Nobody says his name.

[Outro]
This is my flatmate, mother.
This is my—
Sorry. Nothing. Have some cake.
samples.title: This Is My Flatmate - Opus 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Six trophies on the shelf,
Polished up like little men.
He kept the leather on a hook below,
And I know every crack in it by name.
The neighbours brought a lily and a card,
And they queued up in the hall to shake my hand.

[Chorus]
What a gentleman he was,
What a gentleman he was.
Sixteen wins and a shelf full of shine,
And the buckle hanging under.
What a gentleman he was,
And I'm the one who's rude.

[Verse 2]
His flat still smells of Brasso and of smoke,
There's a bible face-down by the chair.
The vicar called him firm but fair,
Said discipline is love in working clothes.
I'm bagging up his shirts by half past four,
And not one of them fits anyone I know.

[Chorus]
What a gentleman he was,
What a gentleman he was.
Sixteen wins and a shelf full of shine,
And the buckle hanging under.
What a gentleman he was,
And I'm the one who's rude.

[Post-Chorus]
Under the shine,
Under the shine,
Under the shine,
That's where I was.

[Bridge]
So say it to my face,
Say it to my face,
Say the belt was only love —
Then give me back my ninth year.

[Chorus]
What a gentleman he was,
What a gentleman he was.
Sixteen wins and a shelf full of shine,
And the buckle hanging under.
What a gentleman he was,
And I'm the one who's rude.

[Outro]
What a gentleman.
What a gentleman.
What a gentleman.
And I'm the one who's rude.
samples.title: What A Gentleman He Was - Opus 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
I kept your jacket in my car.
Six years now, still your cologne.
I rehearsed it every Sunday.
It ended in a door slam.

[Chorus]
This isn't your pardon.
The door's unlocked, you can go.
I'm not forgiving you for you.
This isn't your pardon.

[Verse 2]
I've been feeding it like a furnace.
Since the night you broke my face.
The fire's out and I've lost my faith.
I keep the match in my pocket.

[Chorus]
This isn't your pardon.
The door's unlocked, you can go.
I'm not forgiving you for you.
This isn't your pardon.

[Bridge]
You don't get a seat in my life.
I'm not even angry anymore.
I keep your name like a spare key.
I'll never use it.

[Chorus]
This isn't your pardon.
The door's unlocked, you can go.
I'm not forgiving you for you.
This isn't your pardon.

[Outro - Chant]
The door's unlocked, you can go.
The door's unlocked, you can go.
The door's unlocked, you can go.
samples.title: The Door's Unlocked - Qwen3.8 27b

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
They sang at me. I stood and let them.
That is what a person does.
Then someone put a record on,
And I took a plate outside.

[Chorus]
Out here with the flowerpots and cake,
Where the deckchairs get put away.
I'll come in when they ask for their coats,
Out here with the flowerpots and cake.

[Verse 2]
The shed smells of creosote and seeds.
A wasp goes round the light.
I can hear them doing the accents that they do,
And laughing in the right places.

[Chorus]
Out here with the flowerpots and cake,
Where the deckchairs get put away.
I'll come in when they ask for their coats,
Out here with the flowerpots and cake.

[Guitar Solo]

[Bridge]
Nobody has noticed, which is not a complaint.
I'd rather that they didn't. I'd rather that they did.

[Verse 3]
There's a bag of bulbs from years ago
That someone meant to plant.
I'm thirty-eight. I've eaten all the icing.
The light is going off the greenhouse glass.

[Chorus]
Out here with the flowerpots and cake,
Where the deckchairs get put away.
I'll come in when they ask for their coats,
Out here with the flowerpots and cake.

[Outro]
Sorry — I'll be in.
In a minute.
samples.title: Out Here With The Flowerpots - Opus 5 (1M context)

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Quarter past eleven, the waltzer winds down.
Your car faces out and your engine is off.
Boot packed with the same bags, the same tired tape.
Petrol light on since April — some getaway.

[Pre-Chorus]
So say it slow, say it again.
Tell me the road, tell me when.
You keep the key turned halfway, mate,
and the fair packs down like a riot in reverse.

[Chorus]
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.
You're not stuck in the town, you're stuck in the speech.
Stuck in the speech, and you know it.
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.

[Verse 2]
You practised that goodbye on the back field at fifteen.
Now you say it to a windscreen that never argues.
Your mum still makes your bed, your boss still keeps your shift,
and every year the bags come back inside.

[Chorus]
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.
You're not stuck in the town, you're stuck in the speech.
Stuck in the speech, and you know it.
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.

[Bridge]
I'm not asking you to stay.
I'm asking you to stop rehearsing.
Turn the key or come inside,
'cause the fair's gone home and I'm standing here.

[Chorus]
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.
You're not stuck in the town, you're stuck in the speech.
Stuck in the speech, and you know it.
Third fair in a row, still in the car park.
Still in the car park, saying you're gone.

[Outro]
Still in the car park.
Still in the car park.
Still in the car park.
Still in the car park.
Still in the car park.
Still in the car park.
samples.title: Third Fair In A Row - Opus 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Found a stub in your coat pocket, Tuesday matinee,
Row H, two seats, some film I never asked to see,
I did the sums on the dates, they don't add up to me,
Half of me already knew before I checked the receipt.

[Chorus]
Two seats, no me,
Two seats, and no me,
You bought a ticket for a stranger, honey, not for me,
Two seats, no me.

[Verse 2]
Popcorn on the till slip, timed at half past eight,
I was on the sofa, staring at repeat,
You said you were at your mother's, working late,
The dotted line's signed different from what you told me.

[Chorus]
Two seats, no me,
Two seats, and no me,
You bought a ticket for a stranger, honey, not for me,
Two seats, no me.

[Bridge]
(What's his name?) I don't need it, I can guess.
(Was it good?) The film, or was it him instead.
I'm not asking questions I already know the answer to.

[Verse 3]
I've kept the stub inside my wallet, don't know why,
A little paper alibi that finally cracked the lie,
Now every time you say you're busy, I just smile,
And picture Row H, empty, waiting on the aisle.

[Chorus]
Two seats, no me,
Two seats, and no me,
You bought a ticket for a stranger, honey, not for me,
Two seats, no me.

[Outro]
Two seats, no me,
Two seats, no me,
Row H, two seats, no me.
samples.title: Two Seats, No Me - Sonnet 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Chorus]
Three floors up, and I let you pour,
Three floors up, I don't ask what for,
Your hand stays right where it landed,
Three floors up, I don't leave the floor.

[Verse 1]
Glass, glass, another glass,
You keep it filled before I ask,
The city drops away below,
Every window a small task,
Your fingers find my waist again,
I let them stay, I let them last.

[Chorus]
Three floors up, and I let you pour,
Three floors up, I don't ask what for,
Your hand stays right where it landed,
Three floors up, I don't leave the floor.

[Build - Rising Synth]

[Verse 2]
Words, words, I'm already choosing,
The sorry I'll owe come morning,
Something about a long night working,
Something borrowed, never returning,
The ice keeps melting in my cup,
And still I let you keep on pouring.

[Chorus]
Three floors up, and I let you pour,
Three floors up, I don't ask what for,
Your hand stays right where it landed,
Three floors up, I don't leave the floor.

[Outro - Instrumental]
samples.title: Three Floors Up - Sonnet 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
The porch light's on and you left it on for me,
Eight minutes now and I still won't cut the key.
I've got the whole apology rehearsed and lined up straight,
Every word in order but I can't unlock the gate.
The radio's still playing something neither of us likes,
I keep my hand on the wheel like I'm about to drive.
The dash clock ticks past the hour we stopped talking,
And I'm still sitting here deciding if I'm staying.

[Pre-Chorus]
I count the seconds like they owe me something back,
I check the rearview for a reason to reverse the track.
The house key feels like more than it's ever been,
I don't know how to walk back into a fight I can't win.

[Chorus]
I've got the engine running and the words stuck in my throat,
Thirty feet from the door and I still can't get there, though.
(Engine running.)

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Chorus]
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Scanner's crackling, "shots reported," about.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Sirens somewhere, and I got my doubts.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Get in the car when you hear me shout!

[Verse 1]
Betting shop's shut, the shutter's half down,
Same three faces from the tote round.
Told him nine, he swore on his nan,
Now the till bell's ringing like a countdown plan.
Scanner says "units, respond to the Fox,"
My hands are sweatin' on the gearbox.
Woman walks her dog past, gives me a look,
I'm starin' at a door like it owes me money.

[Chorus]
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Scanner's crackling, "shots reported," about.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Sirens somewhere, and I got my doubts.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Get in the car when you hear me shout!

[Verse 2]
He said the till was fuller than planned,
Some bloke wouldn't drop his where he stand,
Now there's shoutin' comin' from the door,
Two more faces duckin' for the floor.
Scanner's callin' units to the Fox,
I'm still sat here waitin' on the clock.
Alarm goes off, and the shutter jumps,
Here he comes now, runnin' like he's dumped.

[Chorus]
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Scanner's crackling, "shots reported," about.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Sirens somewhere, and I got my doubts.
Ten minutes gone, and he ain't come out,
Get in the car when you hear me shout!

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Phone rang at one, and I already knew,
Your voice came in thin, like the line might drop too,
You said they let you go with a box and a form,
Standin' in the parking lot out in the storm.
I said, sit yourself down at that kitchen table, girl,
Pour the coffee out, we ain't drinkin' tonight,
Put your hand on the wood where the coffee rings curl,
This is a call that always gets answered right.

[Chorus]
Dial it slow, say it plain,
Kitchen table prayer, nine one one for the soul,
Dial it slow, call His name,
That line's always open, He already knows.

[Verse 2]
Say "Lord, I'm tired," don't dress it up nice,
Say the rent is due Friday and you already know the price,
Say her name out loud if you're too proud for advice,
Say, "I need Your hand," and don't ask Him twice.
We went line by line like a bill that's overdue,
Every worry got spoken so it wasn't stuck in you,
And when we ran out of words, we just breathed for a spell,
Table lamp burnin' low, and I swear I could tell.

[Chorus]
Dial it slow, say it plain,
Kitchen table prayer, nine one one for the soul,
Dial it slow, call His name,
That line's always open, He already knows.

[Bridge]
You don't need a suit on, don't need Sunday clothes,
Just a chair and a window and the porch light glow,
He was pickin' up before the second ring,
Before you said a word, He heard everything.

[Chorus]
Dial it slow, say it plain,
Kitchen table prayer, nine one one for the soul,
Dial it slow, call His name,
That line's always open, He already knows.

[Outro]
Call me anytime, but you already got the number,
Call Him anytime, you already got the number,
One more time now, say it, say it, say it,
He already knows, and He already knows.
samples.title: Nine One One for the Soul - Sonnet 5

samples.lyrics:
[Intro - Instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Headlights sweep the ceiling of the car, and neither of us says a word,
Every joke I told at the party plays back louder than I heard,
I trace the seams along the door handle, keeping both hands where they lie,
And the radio sits an inch away, but I don't reach, and I don't try.

[Chorus]
I never touched the radio dial.
(You could have asked me first.)
Thirty-four minutes of quiet denial,
I never touched the radio dial.
(You could have asked me first.)
Rehearsing sorry till it got worse.

[Verse 2]
You caught my eye once at the light, and I stared hard at my knees,
Running back through every word I slurred, apologizing under my breath,
Thinking of the perfect thing to say now, three whole streets too late,
So I let the silence keep on driving, and I let it seal my fate.

[Chorus]
I never touched the radio dial.
(You could have asked me first.)
Thirty-four minutes of quiet denial,
I never touched the radio dial.
(You could have asked me first.)
Rehearsing sorry till it got worse.

[Outro]
I never touched the radio dial.
I never touched the radio dial.
I never touched the radio dial.
I never touched the radio dial.
samples.title: The Radio Dial - Sonnet 5
